subject: Computer Networking
title: Antennas and Signal Strength
description: One-minute skill: Antennas and Signal Strength.

hook.text: Hold your phone differently and your signal changes. The antenna's orientation and surroundings matter enormously.

buildup.text: An antenna converts electrical signals to radio waves and vice versa. Its size is tuned to the target frequency.

discovery.text: Directional antennas focus energy one way for range. Omnidirectional ones radiate equally in all directions.

twist.text: MIMO uses multiple antennas simultaneously. More antennas means more data streams and better reliability.

climax.text: Modern routers have four or eight MIMO antennas. Your phone has at least two. Antenna arrays power modern wireless.

punchline.text: The antenna is the gateway. Better antennas mean better connections.

quiz.question: What does MIMO technology achieve?
options: Multiple simultaneous data streams using multiple antennas
Longer battery life for mobile devices

details.summary: Antennas convert electrical signals to radio waves and vice versa. Omnidirectional antennas radiate equally in all directions, while directional antennas focus energy toward a target.
details.whyItMatters: Antenna selection and placement determine wireless coverage and performance. Understanding antenna types and signal propagation helps optimize network design for any environment.
takeaways: Omnidirectional antennas provide 360-degree coverage for general use
Directional antennas focus energy for longer range in one direction
Antenna gain is measured in dBi relative to an isotropic radiator

faq.question: What is antenna gain?
faq.answer: Gain measures how much an antenna concentrates radio energy in a particular direction compared to an isotropic radiator that radiates equally everywhere. A 6 dBi antenna focuses energy four times more effectively than an isotropic source.

faq.question: How does antenna placement affect signal strength?
faq.answer: Placing antennas higher reduces ground-level obstruction. Central placement in a building maximizes coverage. Walls, metal surfaces, and water absorb or reflect signals. Orienting antennas vertically provides the best coverage in a horizontal plane.
